title: GPU Ops Lighthouse Notes — 2026-10-19
content:
Context: weekly lighthouse sync for GPU fleet ops — focus this week on regional friction, short-term runway, and two A/B priming experiments. These are rough notes from 2026-10-19 meeting (post-standup tidy).

Summary:
- Fleet snapshot (2026-10-19 08:00 PT): total GPUs ~12,900 (H100: 5,100, A100: 4,800, L40: 3,000). Allocated to customers: 73%. Reserved for Dedicated: 14% (enterprise pools). Burst-capacity available: ~9% headroom assuming preemption tolerance.
- Hot regions: eu-west-1 saw sustained >92% utilization between 06:00–11:00 UTC due to a simultaneous batch embed job from two customers. ap-southeast-1 had transient priming latency spikes during morning window.
- Preemption/incidents: single preemption cascade in us-east-1 at 02:50 UTC — caused ~18s latency tail for in-flight streams, root cause traced to zone-level hypervisor upgrade + improper drain timing.

Observations:
- Spot/preemptible backfill working, but shadow queues are growing in eu-west. We need a better tagging rule to avoid backfill on dedicated-latent pools.
- Prewarming A (predictive start based on daily cadence) versus Prewarming B (short-burst start on first request pattern). A reduces cold-start token latency by ~35% for enterprise jobs; B is better for tail latency on small interactive requests.
- Cold KV cache misses contribute ~11% of additional token cost on chat-heavy routes.

Decisions & Priorities:
- Short-term (next 2 weeks): Increase reserved enterprise buffer in eu-west by +120 GPUs (allocate from global spare pool). Rationale: recurring enterprise job conflicts and SLA signals.
- Enable prewarming A for dedicated enterprise pools in ap-southeast-1 as an experiment (rollout window: 2026-10-22 -> 2026-11-05).
- Do NOT expand H100 procurement this quarter; focus on better utilization of existing L40s for embedding workloads.

Action items:
- Ravi: implement tagging rule to block backfill on "enterprise-latent" pools and add coverage test (ticket INFRA-2345). ETA 2026-10-23.
- Leah: schedule controlled drain test in us-east-1 to reproduce hypervisor upgrade timing and update runbook. Link to runbook draft: CAP-1123. ETA 2026-10-25.
- Omar: deploy prewarming A flags to ap-southeast-1 dedicated pool (feature flag PR #478). Monitor 48h and capture priming latency histogram. ETA 2026-10-22.
- Nina: produce short-run forecast with 2-weeks lookahead, include regional risk band (high/medium/low) and show cost delta if we reserve +120 GPUs. Deliver by 2026-10-21.

Metrics to watch (owner):
- Regional utilization 5m moving avg (Ravi)
- Cold-start tail p99 token latency (Leah)
- Preemption rate per-zone (Omar)
- Shadow queue length by pool (Nina)

Risks / Notes-to-self:
- If eu-west enterprise reservations increase, we may push more burst requests into us-west which has a longer network RTT for EMEA customers — watch for quality regressions (latency + hallucination noise when tokens arrive late).
- Current autoscaler cooldown is 60s and may not be optimal for bursty small requests; consider 30s experiment for interactive routes.
- Headcount note: with SRE rotation shrinking for Nov, push more runbook automation before on-call gaps.

Open questions:
- Should we prioritize automated KV cache prefill for top-10 customer prefixes? (cost vs quality trade-off) — proposal due next sync.
- Can we move small-embedding workloads to L40-only pools and tune quantization to reduce cost without impacting throughput? (Leah + Research to evaluate)

Meeting artifacts and links:
- Weekly dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/gpu-capacity?view=weekly
- Incident log (us-east retry): https://redwood.atlassian.net/secure/Incident/INFRA-6347
- Runbook draft: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/CAP-1123

Next sync: 2026-10-26 08:00 PT. Bring histograms for prewarming A/B (Omar) and cost delta table for reserved +120 GPUs (Nina).

Loose notes / brainstorm snippets:
- "lighthouse" idea: visual flag in console for regions in unstable states (amber/red) that surface prewarming candidate pools + quick-reserve button.
- Warm-shed: small ephemeral pool that holds ~200 L40s to absorb bursty embed storms — simulation required.
- TODO: pull sample customer job manifest to simulate eu-west batch collision locally (Ravi)

End.
